name: Lamp / Bulb
tagline: Turns live current into light — and the perfect first circuit to understand the live/neutral path.
parts: Glass envelope — shape and gas atmosphere
Cap / base — bayonet (B22) or Edison screw (E27)
Centre contact + outer thread — live and neutral lands
safety: Never touch the glass of a hot halogen with bare fingers — skin oil creates hot spots that crack it. Match the wattage to the fixture's label.

points.label: Filament / chip
points.detail: The light source — an incandescent filament glows by resistance; an LED 'chip' converts diode forward voltage into light. Modern fittings use the thermal and luminous LED chip, which is why they have a driver, not a filament.

points.label: Glass envelope
points.detail: Sealed glass holds a vacuum or inert gas for a filament (stopping oxidation) or a phosphor coating for LEDs. Some low-energy lamps carry a mercury warning — dispose of them at a recycling point.

points.label: Cap / base
points.detail: Bayonet (B22) has two pins you push-and-twist; Edison screw (E27) threads in. The type is stamped on the lamp base and must match the fitting — they are not interchangeable.

points.label: Centre contact + outer thread
points.detail: Two separate electrical lands: the centre contact is LIVE, the outer thread (or shell) is NEUTRAL. Swapping the lamp wiring makes the accessible metal live when you unscrew the bulb — always land neutral to the shell.

points.label: Rating marking
points.detail: Wattage, voltage, base type and maker are printed on the glass or cap. Match voltage (230 V vs 12 V) and rated draw when replacing lamps for dimmer compatibility.
